_comment: [PROG-20260905-RATCHET] The growth ratchet for the spine reduction program.
Ceilings are measured with z-test/lib/code-line-census.ts and enforced by
z-test/unit/code-line-census.spec.ts. The numbers may only ever go DOWN, and only
in the same commit as the cut that earned the reduction. A rise is a NAMED red:
new logic belongs in its own file behind a short call site (owner order 03/09),
never as a new inline block in the spine.
Program target: methodCodeCeiling <= 1412 crosses the owner's >50% floor;
the committed stop is Phase 5 (~1040-1100). See webhook_spine_reduction_program.md.

SP3 (step zero): maskToken + asString moved to logging/coerce-mask.util.ts. File ceiling 4290 -> 4273. The METHOD ceiling is unchanged at 2829 on purpose: the helpers lived at module scope, so step zero is a prerequisite for later cuts, not a reduction of the method itself.
SP6 (C3): member sync + LINE profile upsert -> room-bootstrap/sync-member-profile.ts. Method 2829 -> 2792 (-37, first real reduction). File 4273 -> 4237.

SP7 (C4): out-of-hours reply -> hook-reply/out-of-hours-reply.handler.ts. Method 2792 -> 2771. NOTE: the first shape of this cut made the method GROW by 2 (the deps-lambda call site was longer than the body) and the ratchet caught it. Rows are built INSIDE the handler; only primitives cross the boundary.

SP8 (C1): tagged-image carousel -> hook-reply/tagged-image-reply.handler.ts. Method 2771 -> 2659 (-112, the biggest single cut so far). It was also the service's only user of axios and objectRuntimeScopeFilter, so both imports left the file with it.
SP9 (C5): credentials + vendor pair -> ai-vendors/request-credentials.ts. Method 2659 -> 2629. docId and logContext assign back to the method-scope lets because the OUTER CATCH reads both.
SP10 (C2): assist state + auto-unassist -> assist/assist-state.gate.ts. Method 2629 -> 2545. Phase 1 (C3,C4,C5,C1,C2) complete: 2829 -> 2545 = 10.0% of the method removed.
SP12: telegram no-answer notify -> assist/telegram-no-answer-notify.ts. Method -> 2533.

SP14 (G35): api-error refusal (helper door S4) -> hook-reply/api-error-reply.handler.ts. Method 2533 -> 2504. Both helper-stamp-doors censuses were converted first — the verify box was right that there are THREE assertions in that spec, not two.
SP15 (G34): prompt assembly -> ai-reply/prompt-assembly.ts. Method 2504 -> 2466. The model call stayed in the spine: when it fires is a gate-order fact.
SP16: the two post-send webhook_log rows -> logging/send-outcome-rows.ts. Method 2466 -> 2447. The error row's request_meta was nearly dropped in the copy — caught by diffing against the original.
SP17 (G16b): combined profile fetch -> room-bootstrap/combined-profile.ts. Method 2447 -> 2335. NINE outputs, not eight: profileCircuitOpen was missed by a mechanical scan and caught by tsc.

SP18 (G22): the postback rule and the swallow -> room-bootstrap/inbound-chat-row.ts. Method 2335 -> 2333: only -2, because the row literal stays in the spine which owns its values. Kept for the ORGANISATION, not the size — the NOPOSTBACKROW rule is now a named unit instead of a comment inside a try.

SP20 (G44): flex-history rewrite -> post-send/flex-history-rewrite.ts. Method 2333 -> 2283. Unlocked by converting two pins first (customer-helper-flex-history reads across role dirs; its ROOMPREVIEW cases match either `this.` or `deps.` because the collaborator prefix was never the rule).

SP21 (G27): openAdminCaseDirect -> ticket/open-admin-case.ts. Method 2283 -> 2214. Unlocked by converting admin-direct-ticket first: its DOOR slice now spans the seat in the spine PLUS the extracted body, because the seat and the body legitimately live in different files after the cut.

SP22 (G25): assist bypass -> non-text/assist-bypass.ts. Method 2214 -> 2151 = 24.0% removed. formatThaiDateTime moved to logging/coerce-mask.util.ts with it (a role file cannot call a module-private function). Three pins converted to keep their rules across the move: the slip twin normaliser folds `this.`/`deps.` and `meta.`/`args.` prefixes, and slip-flex-lock-duplicate-first counts both sites across files.

SP23 (G23): follow-up flow -> gates/follow-up-flow.ts (NOT follow-up/: that module must not import register/, and follow-up-boundaries.spec.ts refused the wrong placement). Method 2151 -> 2102 = 25.7% removed. z-test/lib/spine-sources.ts now holds the shared 'spine plus role dirs' reader after five hand-rolled copies.

SP25: the incoming_line_webhook row -> logging/incoming-delivery-row.ts as a PURE BUILDER (the emit stays in the spine, because the fire-and-forget void is the spine's contract). Method 2102 -> 2095. It qualified where the other wlog literals did not: nine fields out, four inputs in. SP24 called the free pool exhausted for BLOCKS; the rule that actually decides a row extraction is fields >> inputs, and the reply rows fail it (10 lines of arguments to replace 12 lines of literal). Same commit: buildRoomFilter, which had grown FOUR identical copies (three of them created BY this program, because a role file cannot call a module-private helper), consolidated into room-bootstrap/room-filter.ts. File 3532 -> 3518. That is destination bloat repaid, not new reduction.

SP27: the assist turn context. `runAssistGuarded` is called from THREE places in the spine and nineteen of each literal's ~24 fields carried byte-identical expressions — one fact written down three times. Replaced by one arrow (`assistTurn()`) typed by assist/assist-turn-args.ts. Method 2095 -> 2054, file 3527 -> 3487. It MUST be an arrow, not a value: nine of the nineteen come from `let`s the turn reassigns (customerName at four sites, bangkokTime at three), and the call sites are 1,000-2,000 lines below the definition, so a value would freeze stale data with every test still green. tsc rejected the first version of the type — telegramKey is `string | null | undefined` upstream — which is exactly the check a shared type is for.

SP28 (G19): the unlinked-slip refusal -> hook-reply/unlinked-slip-refusal.handler.ts. Method 2054 -> 1975 = 30.2% removed, file 3487 -> 3407. 154 CODE of branch replaced by a 90-line call site. It only became worth moving AFTER SP27 shrank its assist tail from 24 lines to 4 - before that it was the G22 shape (a move that relocates a literal). Two pins converted (refused-helper-flex, abandon-trigger) and one census taught two things it was silently getting wrong: it counted a doc COMMENT quoting the pattern as a door, and a deps BINDING as a call site. The collaborator name buildHookHelperFlexFor is kept identical across the boundary on purpose - renaming it made that census see three doors instead of four.

SP29 (G45): the AI send + its four post-send records -> ai-reply/send-ai-reply.handler.ts. Method 1975 -> 1861 = 34.2% removed, file 3407 -> 3286. The guards ABOVE it stayed in the spine (empty-reply return, staleness guard): when a gate fires is a gate-order fact. The handler RETHROWS on a failed send, exactly as the block did, so the outer catch still writes its handle_webhook row. Six orphaned imports moved with it - each one checked against every patch by name after the pre-flight was found to be skipping multi-line import blocks silently.

SP30 (G31): the missing-profile-data reply (helper door S2) -> hook-reply/missing-profile-data-reply.handler.ts. Method 1861 -> 1824 = 35.5% removed. Deliberately NOT merged with its twin api-error-reply.handler.ts: four behaviours differ (log line, empty-field fallback text, action_type, and the history row - the twin files text even when a card went out, which its own header records as fossilized because the abandon lookback reads that field). Also this save point: free-block-sweep.py, which asks the whole method at once instead of one block at a time, after reading produced two wrong answers in a row.

SP31 (AIROW): the generate_response audit row -> logging/ai-audit-row.ts as a pure builder. Method 1824 -> 1807 = 36.1% removed. The fourth and largest of the four webhook_log rows a turn can produce, now all in logging/ where they can be read side by side. Four helpers went with it as orphaned imports. The `void` stays at the call site because WHEN it is written is the spine contract (PERF-20260824-WLOGVOID).

SP32 (DOCFETCH + ERRTEXT): the doc-retrieval decision -> doc-retrieval/fetch-related-text.ts, beside the seam and adapter it drives. Method 1807 -> 1794 = 36.6% removed. Also: errText had TWELVE identical copies (ten created by this program) and now has one home in logging/coerce-mask.util.ts, with a census. The pre-flight EARNED ITS KEEP this save point by refusing a cut: :2823-2898 would orphan upgradeTicketCategoryOnSlip, which is a menu-plug context byte - the G20 trap, caught before any file was touched.

SP35 (LADDER L1+L2a): the gate ladder itself. Method 1794 -> 1754 = 38.0% removed, file 3212 -> 3189. The dive that preceded it corrected the tool that had reported 25 rungs: the method holds 65 guards, and the 39 the old scan hid are inside `if (userId)`, which is 934 CODE. What is left in the spine after thirty save points of body-moving is the ORDER and the WIRING, both expressed only as physical line position — which is why the order could only be defended in prose (1,598 comment lines against 1,794 code lines) and why 29 collaborator names were bound more than once for 136 lines, 107 of them redundant. This save point lands `gates/`: a step contract, a runner, ONE turn-deps object bound per turn, and the first four steps (out-of-hours, registered-event, require-user-text, api-error-trigger). Only -40 because `turnDeps()` is a one-time investment; it is what makes every later slice cheaper. The part that matters is not the size: each step DECLARES what it must follow or precede and why, and `gate-ladder-order.spec.ts` proves the shipped order satisfies all of them - including the rule that out-of-hours must stay BELOW the non-text branch, or a switched-off OA stops answering images. That rule was a comment until now. A step still inline in the spine is declared in INLINE_ABOVE_TAIL with its line and its side, so a constraint may point at it and a TYPO still fails - a fence that cannot fail is not a fence. Also: `gates` was missing from SPINE_ROLE_DIRS since SP23 put follow-up-flow.ts there, a hole in every fence built on the default list.

SP36 (LADDER L2b): the model lane becomes eight ladder steps. Method 1754 -> 1547 = 45.3% removed, file 3189 -> 3033. 451 lines of spine replaced by twelve: document retrieval, the model turn, the api-error refusal, the reply-text choice, the bot's chat row, the audit row, the Telegram page and the assist hand-off. The wins compound the way the design predicted - SP35's turnDeps() was a 17-line investment and this save point spent nothing on wiring, because `log`/`error`/`emitWlog`/`logMessageAwaited` were already bound once for the turn. Three rules that were prose are now machine-checked: substitution AFTER retrieval (retrieval caches by doc_id, so substituting first makes the cached body hook-specific and two hooks sharing a document read each other's domain), the api-error refusal only AFTER the model has answered, and the assist hand-off after both the resolved text and the row it links. TWO NEAR-MISSES CAUGHT: `resolveDictTool` was first re-implemented inline as `typeof value === 'string'` instead of importing `asString` - `custom_tool_id` is an ObjectId, so every OA with a bound tool would silently have lost its vocabulary with nothing failing to compile; and tsc refused a widened `tagStatus: string`, which is exactly what a shared type is for. `creds` travels as ONE object rather than fifteen unpacked names - unpacking fifteen to hand eight straight back down was the same re-bind-at-every-site habit the turn-deps object exists to end.

SP39 (LADDER L4): the reply tail becomes the ladder's SECOND slice. Method 1547 -> 1441 = 49.1% removed, file 3033 -> 2962. Five steps: the TAG-STRIP probe, the flex_pc safe text, the empty-reply return, the staleness guard and the send. THE LADDER IS NOW IN TWO PIECES, and that is a plug patch rather than a design choice: the flex-card build between them is ONE expression whose tail is a menu-plug box owning `flexKind === 'menu'`, `tags.wantedMenuCardTag`, `flexOut` and the closing `: null) ?? null) as Record<string, unknown> | null;` as BYTES - so those names must stay locals of the method, and an expression cannot be cut in half. The build moves at Phase 5 or not at all. The same ctx and the same deps are reused, so resuming costs one line. 🔴 THE CUT BROKE THE MENU PATCH ONCE: the hunk's trailing context is the `: null)` line PLUS a blank line PLUS the first line of the AIPROMPTLOG comment, and the replacement deleted the last two. `git apply --check -R` caught it - the G20 trap, caught by the gate rather than by reading. Those three lines now carry a 🔴 note. Also: the order and data-chain fences are checked over the CONCATENATION of both slices, never slice by slice, because `send-ai-reply mustFollow bot-chat-row` is an edge from the second slice back into the first and validating separately would drop every such edge while still reporting green.

SP40 (LADDER L5): the reply tags, the tag-based image carousel and the customer-helper swap. Method 1441 -> 1402 = 50.4% removed — THE OWNER'S >50% FLOOR IS CROSSED, and with no plug byte touched. Three steps join the FIRST slice; what comes back to the spine are only the values the FROZEN flex build reads by name. `tags` must stay a local spelled exactly that way because `tags.wantedMenuCardTag` is a byte of docs/menu-plug-in.patch. THE ORDER FENCE EARNED ITSELF THIS SAVE POINT: `helper-qr-body` sits in the first slice and declares `mustPrecede: ['require-something-to-send']`, which lives in the SECOND — checked against the first array alone the fence threw 'names nothing', correctly, and the fix was to check the CONCATENATION, because two slices interrupted by a patch box are still one ladder. Every shipped-order case now reads FULL_LADDER for that reason.

SP43 (LADDER L6): the turn context moves to the TOP of the method, and the prologue becomes the ladder's first slice. Method 1402 -> 1374 = 51.4% removed, file 2929 -> 2916. THE LIFT ON ITS OWN COSTS +8 CODE AND THE RATCHET REFUSED IT — correctly; the method ceiling has no raise mechanism and must never get one. It was parked in a stash and landed only when paired with the cut it enables. That is the whole discipline working as designed. WHY IT HAD TO MOVE: a step can only read a context that already exists, so while the context was built just above the first runLadder call, NOTHING ABOVE THAT LINE COULD EVER BECOME A STEP — the entire head and every gate inside `if (userId)` was locked in place by the position of one `const`. Three steps landed with it: the signature re-check, the event re-read and the eager room bootstrap. `event` and `userId` lost `readonly`, because the re-read genuinely reassigns them and a modifier that says otherwise is worse than none. The slice STOPS before the payment seat: `if (payPb.handled) return;` is now inside menu-plug-in.patch's box, so that seat and the menu seat below it stay inline and the ladder resumes after them. Three slices, ONE context, ONE deps object. `meta.rawBody` is typed `Buffer | string` against the real shape rather than narrowed to string — the HMAC runs over the exact bytes LINE signed, and a re-serialised body hashes differently, which IS the disagreement the re-check reports.

SP44 (LADDER L7): the customer slice — the two admin doors, the notice guard for ordinary text, the abandon flow and the register keyword. Method 1374 -> 1287 = 54.5% removed, file 2916 -> 2891. FOUR SLICES NOW, one context, one deps object: prologue · customer (inside `if (userId)`) · tail · reply. The slice starts after the rate limiter and stops before the non-text branch, because plug hunks own bytes in both. TWO MISTAKES CAUGHT BY THE GATES RATHER THAN BY READING: (1) the handover that fills profileData/existingUser/skipBotProcessing/inboundRoom still ran BELOW `if (userId)`, so the customer slice would have read the INITIAL values — the notice guard told no operator holds the room, the admin doors finding no room to open a case against, nothing throwing and nothing failing to compile. Moved above the slice. (2) moving that block deleted a comment terminator and COMMENTED OUT THE ENTIRE TAIL LADDER CALL; tsc caught it only because the import went unused. Nine source-text pins converted, and one of them was about to lie: three position cases in follow-up-gate.spec.ts anchored on `indexOf('await runFollowUpFlow()')`, which after the move finds the SILENT-TYPE call — a different site with a different position — so all three would have kept passing while checking a rule nobody wrote. They now anchor on the slice call site and on the ladder array, which is the runtime order.

SP45 (LADDER L9+L10 as one): the media slice — the non-text lane. Method 1287 -> 1153 = 59.2% removed, file 2891 -> 2812. Five steps: the payment run and the slip card, the assist hand-off on the image path, the flex-sent exit, the missing-API-data reply and the media reply text. FIVE SLICES NOW. The slice stops at the send, whose `try` belongs to menu-plug-in.patch (four hunks own the menu card, the stamp, the wlog row and the history row inside it). THE CUT DROPPED TWO THINGS AND BOTH WERE RECOVERED FROM GIT rather than retyped: the branch's own `if (event.type === 'message' && ...)` line — an off-by-one on the slice start, which unbalanced the braces and tsc reported as a missing catch — and the `imgProbe('gate-image-answer')` call, which is capability and not decoration. FOUR PIN CONVERSIONS IN slip-answer-twin-sites.spec.ts, and each is a rule kept rather than a fence widened: the twin count stopped counting `turnDeps` as a call site (it is the ONE wiring site and binds every collaborator once — SP28 hit the same class from the other direction); the argument comparison folds `ctx.<group>.<field>` to the bare name so a field that genuinely disappears still shows as a difference; the slipCondition POSITION rule moved from a text offset to the ladder's declared order, because the write and the read are now in two files and concatenation order is alphabetical accident; and the seven-deps comparison became a per-name check at both sites, because one site's deps are bound once for the turn — stated as a real loss of the ORDER half rather than hidden. Also: the dep was renamed back to `handleSlipCallback` — a collaborator name must stay identical across the boundary or a census reads a moved door as a deleted one.

SP46 (LADDER L9): the image lane's top half — store the picture, pre-scan it for a QR, decide the unlinked-slip refusal. Method 1153 -> 1099 = 61.2% removed, file 2812 -> 2774. THE ORDER IS THE FEATURE HERE, not an arrangement: the owner fixed it on 12/08 after an ordinary photo from an unregistered customer was answered with 'please link your account first' and stopped dead. Each step now names the one before it, so that order is checked instead of defended in prose. The three steps only DECIDE - `blockUnlinked` is computed and deliberately left unused until past the notice guard, because the notice runtime gets the first turn (owner, 24/08); a step that replied here would silently reverse that. THE PRE-FLIGHT CAUGHT WHAT GREP DID NOT: `storageId` is declared inside the cut span and read 340 lines below it, at the verifySlip call - a hand-written grep loop missed it and the tool did not. It also had to stay an ObjectId rather than being narrowed to a hex string: verifySlip writes it into an ObjectId column, so a string would have worked only through a mongoose cast - a behaviour change smuggled in under a type simplification. THREE FAILURES THE FULL SUITE FOUND, and only one was this cut's: (1) MINE - the new slice comment spelled the strike tap's method name, and strike-plug-patch.spec.ts reverts the patch then asserts the reverted file holds no trace of it, so prose alone made the switch look broken; a plug's method name must never appear in a comment. (2) slip-flex-lock-duplicate-first had a HAND-WRITTEN LIST OF TWO FILE PATHS and SP45 moved one of the sites, so it had been asserting toHaveLength(2) against one site since that save point - now spineSource(['gates', 'non-text']), narrowed rather than defaulted because slip-flex/ discusses duplicateFirst in prose. (3) strike-suspend-plug compared the gate against the first `getOrCreateRoom(` in the file, which since SP35 is the line that BINDS the collaborator in turnDeps - a bind is not a write, the same class as the door census that read a binding as a call site at SP28; it now measures against the prologue slice call AND asserts ensure-room is in that slice, because 'above a ladder that no longer contains the write' would guard nothing. Also: `ladderCtx.slip = {...}` at the customer handover became field-by-field assignment - a whole-object literal there would discard everything the image slice wrote onto the context eight hundred lines earlier, and tsc only catches that while the field names differ.

SP47 (LADDER L8): the unlinked-slip refusal's WIRING. Method 1099 -> 1028 = 63.7% removed, file 2774 -> 2715. The BODY moved at SP28; what was left in the spine was a seventeen-field input literal and a nineteen-line deps literal, THIRTEEN of whose collaborators were already bound once for the turn a thousand lines above - the exact duplication turnDeps() exists to end. Four genuinely new deps were added there (buildHookHelperFlexFor, sendFlexReply, stampIfHelperCardDelivered, logSystemMessage) and are now available to every later step. IT IS A SLICE OF ITS OWN, NOT A FOURTH STEP OF THE IMAGE SLICE, and the reason is a patch box: the slip-path notice guard sits between the decision and the reply, its consumeQuota closure holds a strike-plug hunk, and the guard MUST stay between them - [FEAT-20260824-NOTICEFIRST], owner 24/08: an unlinked customer's slip meets the off-hours card before it meets 'please link your account'. Merging the slices would undo that with nothing failing on behaviour. THE DATA-CHAIN FENCE EARNED ITSELF AGAIN: the step reads profileForLog, which the customer handover writes EIGHT HUNDRED LINES BELOW this position - assertDataChain named the field and refused. Without it the refusal would have logged an empty profile on every row, compiling and green. The handover for it went beside the three the image slice already needed. TWO LOG STRINGS KEPT AT THE SITE RATHER THAN IN THE BINDING: deps.logBotMessage(row, tag) produces '<tag> Log failed', but this site has always logged '[REQUIREPROFILE] history log failed', and the divider's line is a whole Thai sentence. Those strings are what an operator greps, so logSystemMessage returns the promise UNCAUGHT and the two catches stay in the step. TWO PINS CONVERTED AND BOTH PROVEN RED: notice-before-requireprofile's REFUSAL anchor was `if (blockUnlinked) {`, now the slice call at the same position; and refused-helper-flex's door regex folds an optional `ctx.` prefix, because the binding moved into turnDeps and reads ctx.hook / ctx.event.source?.userId - the same two values under the name the ladder gives them, the same fold this program applied to this./deps. at SP22. Three stale prose references to `if (blockUnlinked)` in the notice guard's own revert instructions were corrected in the same commit; a revert note that names a statement which no longer exists is a trap, not a note.

SP48 (CTXBUILD + SLICEORDER): the turn context's forty empty seats move to gates/build-turn-context.ts, beside the type that declares them. Method 1028 -> 967 = 65.8% removed, file 2715 -> 2655. The seeds and TurnContext are one fact written twice and they sat two thousand lines apart, so adding a field meant editing ladder.types.ts and then HUNTING for the literal buried in processLockedEvent. `TurnSeed` is a Pick of TurnContext rather than a parallel interface: a second shape would be a contract to keep in sync, and this program has already paid for one of those. AND THE FENCE THAT SHOULD HAVE EXISTED SINCE SP39: every case in gate-ladder-order.spec.ts walks FULL_LADDER and treats its position as the runtime order. That is true only while the spread matches the sequence of runLadder() calls in the spine - two hand-maintained lists in two files. Out of step, assertDataChain would CLEAR a step that really does read a field before anything writes it, because in the array the writer comes first: a fence reporting green while guarding nothing, the exact shape of every bug this program has fixed. The new case derives the slice order from the spine source, so a slice added or moved is picked up without editing it. IT FAILED ON ITS FIRST RUN AND WAS RIGHT TO: read against the raw file it counted unlinked-slip-refuse twice, because the notice guard's revert instruction MENTIONS the call in prose. A comment about a call is not a call - the same mistake the helper-door census made at SP28 - so it now reads code-only lines via classifyLines. Control-tested: swapping two slices in FULL_LADDER turns it red, restoring turns it green. ALSO RECORDED, A CUT THAT WAS REFUSED: the slip verify block (:3016-3105, 38 CODE) cannot move. Extracting it orphans `upgradeTicketCategoryOnSlip`, whose import line is a CONTEXT byte of docs/menu-plug-in.patch (line 240) - delete it and the menu plug stops applying, keep it and tsc fails on an unused import. That is the G20 trap, and the pre-flight named it before any file was touched, for the second time on this same block. It is Phase 5 work or nothing.

SP50 (HANDOVER + G25): the customer handover moves UP ~330 lines to the earliest position that is still correct, and the assist bypass becomes a step. Method 967 -> 924 = 67.3% removed, file 2655 -> 2636. THE HANDOVER MOVE IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. It sat just above the customer slice, far later than any value in it becomes final - and 'later than necessary' is not harmless: a step placed between the last write and the handover reads the context's INITIAL value, compiles, and is silently wrong. That is the same failure the block's own comment already described, one position down. The new position was MEASURED, not guessed: a script checked all eighteen values and found `customerMsg` is the last to be decided, so the statement that writes it is the earliest legal line. Moving earlier would hand over a null customerMsg and the assist ticket's chatMsgId would quietly stop pointing at the customer's own message - so the site now carries that rule, in both directions. G25 (the assist bypass) only became movable BECAUSE of that: six of the sixteen values it forwards - the three slip-verify results, profileData, customerTel and the media url - reached the context ~330 lines BELOW the cut site until this save point. Cutting first would have compiled and handed an operator's room an empty slip result. The step builds its INPUT from the context rather than letting turnDeps bind it, because `reads` is what assertDataChain checks and a fence checking a list the code no longer matches is worse than no fence; the eleven COLLABORATORS are bound once in turnDeps. AND THE POOL IS NOW EMPTY. The free-block sweep finds exactly two patch-free blocks of >=25 CODE left, and BOTH are refused with proof: (1) the paid slip verify orphans `upgradeTicketCategoryOnSlip`, whose import is a context byte of menu-plug-in.patch; (2) the payment postback is blocked TWICE OVER - `handlePaymentPostback`'s import is a context byte of strike-suspend-plug-in.patch line 19, and the block's own exit `if (payPb.handled) return;` plus the two comment lines above it are context bytes of menu-plug-in.patch line 493. Verified by reading the patch hunks directly, not by trusting the tool. => 924 CODE / 67.3% is the practical floor for block-level cuts. Going further is Phase 5 (regenerate the plug patches) or many small cuts below the 25-CODE threshold, neither of which has been dived. The earlier '85% / ~424 CODE' figure priced neither blocker and should not be quoted as a target until Phase 5 is agreed.

OWNER DECISIONS, 05/09 — asked explicitly and answered, recorded here so the next session does not re-open them. (1) PHASE 5 IS DECLINED FOR NOW: the plug patches are NOT regenerated, so the ~330 CODE they freeze stays frozen and 923 CODE / 67.4% is the ACCEPTED STOPPING POINT, not a shortfall. Anyone reading the earlier '85% / ~424 CODE' target should read this line instead: that figure priced neither the menu-patch import trap nor the payPb exit bytes, and it is not a goal any more. (2) `bangkokTime`'s two date formats stay as they are - the owner was shown both (`05 September 2026 at 22:15:30` vs `5/9/2569 22:15:30`, Gregorian vs Buddhist) and chose to leave them; two-writer-locals.spec.ts keeps the divergence visible but it is a settled question, not a pending defect. (3) The multi-event cap is 5 with drop-and-warn on overflow, and the switch stays OFF; tier 2 (flip on locally + live two-event proof) waits on LINE's redelivery switch being enabled. The capability itself is now proven AT the cap rather than inferred from two- and three-event cases.

PHASE 5 DIVE, 05/09 — measured end to end before deciding, and the conclusion is that its premise expired. WHAT IS ACTUALLY FROZEN: three patches, 23 hunks, TEN of them inside processLockedEvent (:1931-4068) holding 246 CODE of feature across 371 raw lines — menu 6 hunks / 229 CODE, strike 3 / 9, strike-suspend 1 / 8. Located by matching each hunk's full line SEQUENCE against the live file; a first attempt matched context lines individually and reported nonsense spans, because a lone `}` matches the first one in the file. ONLY ONE OF THE TEN IS WORTH ANYTHING. menu hunk 8 (:2333-2509) is a real BODY — the engine construction literal, the card-var resolver with its profile closure, the press budget attempt/release, and handlePostback — about 144 CODE. The other nine are seats and read-only taps of 3-18 CODE each; extracting them relocates a literal and buys nothing (the G22 result). TWO FINDINGS THAT CLOSE IT: (1) `webhook_spine_reduction_program.md` projects ~1,040-1,100 CODE = 61-63% AFTER Phase 5. We are at 923 = 67.4% WITHOUT it — past that milestone and inside the doc's own Phase 6 band (~650-880 = 69-77%). The phase was priced as insurance for a floor that has already been cleared. (2) That same document's correction #2 states Phase 5's headline goal is NOT EXPRESSIBLE: 'menu plug becomes a whole-file add, no spine insertion, no context bytes' cannot hold, because the spine must statically import the handler and that import cannot compile in the plug-OFF state — so the call site AND the import remain patch hunks at the same seam. WHAT IT WOULD COST: regenerate the largest off-switch in the repo (812 lines, 13 hunks), rewrite `plug-patch-contract.spec.ts`'s spansOf() for new-file hunks (it readFileSyncs per hunk and ENOENTs in the OFF state; locate() returns -1 on an empty pre-side), and edit `menu-isolation-census.spec.ts`'s ALLOWED_IMPORTERS. The failure mode is not a red test: it is a patch that still applies but no longer reverts, which means the menu quietly loses the off switch that makes `rm -rf src/modules/menu` a complete revert — the property the whole plug design exists to provide. ⇒ PHASE 5 IS CLOSED ON EVIDENCE, not deferred. Reopening it needs a NEW reason: the ~144 CODE prize is real but it is the only one, and the arithmetic that justified the phase is stale. The owner had already declined it on other grounds the same day; this dive agrees with that answer for reasons the owner did not have at the time.

[FEAT-20260907-UNKNOWNPROFILEREVIEW] File ceiling 2630 -> 2631. 🔴 THIS IS A RISE, and the rule above says a rise is a NAMED red — so it is named. The line is ONE dep binding, `findFlexById`, handing the ladder the lookup `resolveStateFlex` needs; the logic it serves lives in gates/unknown-profile-review.step.ts and hook-reply/unknown-profile-review.handler.ts, which is the shape the rule asks for (own file, short call site) rather than the shape it forbids (a new inline block). The METHOD ceiling is unchanged: the binding sits in the ladder deps literal, not in the method under reduction.

The cheaper cut was identified and NOT taken: `findFlexById` is now wired FOUR times in this file (webhook.service.ts:1421, 1542, 1584, 4321) and hoisting it to one member would return ~4-6 lines. It was declined for this change because the four differ (`lean<Record<string,unknown>>` vs `lean<never>`, and two coerce with `String(id)`) and all four sit on the money path — a refactor that deserves its own commit and its own backtest, not a side effect of adding a reply. Whoever takes it: that cut is available and this +1 is the first thing it should pay back.

NOTE for whoever reads this next: the `findFlexById` cut named in the entry above is still available and still unpaid — this change did not take it, and did not need to.
_fileCeilingRaisedBy_comment: The METHOD ceiling may only ever go down; there is no mechanism here to raise it, and
there must never be one. The FILE ceiling is different: the file also holds
`processWebhook`, the constructor and the module-scope helpers, so a genuinely NEW
feature can land there while the method does not move at all. Refusing that outright
does not stop the file growing — it teaches the next person to inline the feature into
an existing block to dodge the counter, which is the exact bloat the ratchet exists to
prevent. So a raise is allowed, and it is made expensive instead of impossible: it must
be listed below, it must name a feature tag that really appears in the file, and it must
state what was added. `code-line-census.spec.ts` checks all three, so a raise cannot be
